blurb: Buckets and the Store files in them.
reasons: Why the family is backup and the thing is a bucket: the calls back up and restore Stores; what they name, list and check is a bucket.
Why the key's secret comes on stdin: a secret in an argument lands in shell history and process listings. The key's id is not a secret and stays an option.
Why list takes --bucket: anything optional is an option.
Why restore puts the bucket first: positionals go from the source to what is made: the bucket, its file, then the Store.
Why a row says behind, not a state word: state is one of six words everywhere. A backup that is behind is a fact about a link, and true is the news.
Why the write test is --full: --with only ever adds a section to an answer; a doctor's deeper check is its Full check (R5).

calls.note: the URL names the provider, the bucket and the prefix, as today: r2://<account>/<bucket>/<prefix> (with ?jurisdiction=) or http(s)://<host>/<bucket>/<prefix>. name is the bucket's name in this home: what a call creates is named name, and every other call takes it as <bucket>. The key's id is --access-key. Its secret is the option secret_key: the shell reads it from stdin with --key-stdin and takes it no other way; Node and Python pass it as the option. It is kept in the home's secret folder (0600), never answered, and the call log records its byte count only, as it does for the URL. It makes one listing before it records anything: Unavailable when the bucket cannot be reached or refuses the key. Its outcome is connected. Connected again under a taken name at the same URL (provider, bucket and prefix equal after parsing, with r2's account and ?jurisdiction= and an endpoint's scheme and host), it replaces the key: the same one listing proves the new key first, and on Unavailable nothing changes; then the secret is saved by one rename and the record's access_key in one record write, and every Store's link to the bucket stays (outcome rotated; the short form is a first connect's). A taken name at another URL is Exists, with the fix layerfs backup disconnect <name>; a new name works too

calls.new_work: `--access-key` and `--key-stdin` are new: today `--key` names a reference (env:NAME or file:/path, default env:LAYERFS_BUCKET_<NAME>) that the caller resolves to an access key and a secret on every call. Keeping the secret in the home's secret folder is new (the same folder store.save_auth needs). The answer's `url` is new: today the record keeps the URL's parts (account or endpoint, bucket, prefix) and answers those.

calls.note: one row per Store file in each connected bucket, and one per link whose file the bucket does not hold (missing:true). store is the Store of this home linked to the file; an unlinked file has none. behind:true: the Store changed since its last backup. changed:true: the file in the bucket is not the one the link last moved. Both are null, with a message, when that could not be read. These three replace today's state word (current, store_changed, bucket_changed, both_changed, unknown, unlinked, missing): state is the six-state word only. A backup that is behind is reported as a notice by store doctor (store.backups), not by a bucket check. A bucket that cannot be listed no longer fails the call: it is named in not_listed, the shape every list uses for what it could not include: {bucket, reason, message}, with reason lost (no listing came back: the bucket did not answer, or refused its key; the message says which) or timeout. The long form's entry also has blocked_by, always null: a bucket waits on nothing. The manifest's exported_from and binding are not answered: reading them is one more request per file. Unpaged: a row per Store file under each bucket's prefix, a handful per bucket; sha256 is read for at most 64 files of one listing and is null past that
calls.help: the Store files in the connected buckets, with the Store each is linked to

short: a bucket that cannot be listed: {"items":[{"bucket":"r2-main","file":"shop","size":213263952,"store":"shop"}],"not_listed":[{"bucket":"minio-lab","reason":"lost","message":"minio-lab did not answer at http://lab:9000"}]}

calls.new_work: A bucket that cannot be listed is tolerated and named in `not_listed`: today one bad bucket fails the whole call. `behind` for a Store on a machine is new: today the Store's heads are read on native only and the row says `unknown`; it needs one read through the machine's worker (the same read as store.get --with live). `sha256` exists in the listing and is not answered today.

calls.note: sqlite only (a PostgreSQL Store is InvalidInput). Copies a consistent snapshot of the Store to the bucket and links the two. The file is named after the Store unless --file says otherwise. A file another home wrote is Exists; a file that is not the copy this home last moved is Conflict, and nothing is uploaded. Phases: check, snapshot, send (from a machine to this computer, bytes), hash, upload (bytes). Today's pieces counts are gone from the answer and the events. A failure leaves the link as it was, and attempt on the Store's backup row says what was tried. A lost reply to the upload is Unknown: the file may or may not be replaced, and nothing is resent. The Store is then broken, unresolved until layerfs store get <store> --with live settles it: a backup changes nothing in the Store, so the read drops the op. A snapshot a killed backup left beside the Store is removed by the next backup create of that Store, or a backup restore that replaces it (v20)
calls.help: back up a sqlite Store to a bucket

options.name: file
options.help: the file's name in the bucket; the Store's name when left out

calls.new_work: Recording the backup as the Store's `op` (name `backup`) is new, so every client sees `busy`: today it holds the Store's lease and a file lock and records nothing, so today nothing is left to clear after a lost reply. With the `op`, an uncertain backup whose owner is gone is settled by `store get --with live` (new work; see store.get). The link's `attempt` record is new. The {phase, done, total} events replace today's events with `pieces: {done, of}`.

calls.note: reads file from the bucket into the sqlite Store store on this computer (native): a new Store (outcome created), or it replaces an idle Store on native that is unchanged since its last backup or restore through this bucket (outcome replaced). A Store that changed since is Conflict, one in use is InUse, one on another machine is Unsupported (move it to native first), as today. Positionals go source first: bucket, file, then the Store. projects are the projects found in it (first 20). Phases: check, download (bytes), verify, install. The install is one rename; a restore whose reply is lost while it replaces a Store leaves it broken, unresolved until layerfs store get <store> --with live settles it. A killed restore's staging folder is removed by the next restore, as today
calls.help: restore a Store file from a bucket as a sqlite Store on this computer

dropped.why: a restore names the file it reads; today it is the Store's linked file, else its name, when left out

calls.new_work: Recording the restore as the Store's `op` (name `restore`) is new when it replaces an existing Store: today it works under the home lock and a locked staging folder and records nothing. With the `op`, an uncertain restore whose owner is gone is settled by `store get --with live` (new work; see store.get). The positional order changes from <store> <bucket> [file]; nothing else is new.

calls.note: one bucket, by the checks of checks.bucket in order: its configuration, its key, that it answers, and one listing page under its prefix. --full (R5) also writes one small object, reads it back and deletes it (the full_only checks; bucket.reconcile runs only after a put whose reply was lost); the node's coverage is then full. Without --full those checks are left out of the report, not listed as skipped. A backup that is behind is not a bucket check: store doctor reports it (store.backups). The tree is the bucket's one node. Today's ids were backup.*, all kept under bucket.*: a check is named after the thing it checks. Exits 0 once the report is made

calls.new_work: The call is new on the table; its checks exist as today's `layerfs doctor backup connection <bucket>` (backup.configuration, credentials, transport, list, and write_capability, put, get, delete, reconcile behind --write-test). New: the `bucket.*` ids, the one answer shape (a check that was not asked for is left out, where today it is listed as skipped), and the bucket's own time budget in place of --timeout.
